INITIAL cursor: cols 15-19 (under P-symbol 0)
CURRENT cursor: cols 22-26 (under P-symbol 1)
The cursor moved from P-symbol 0 to P-symbol 1 after pressing UP. And P-symbol 1 was transformed.
So it seems like:
- The cursor starts at P-symbol 0 (bottom position)
- UP moves the cursor right to the next symbol AND transforms that symbol
- The cursor has two positions: one between S and P palettes (rows 48-49) and one below P palette (rows 59-60)
Wait, but both positions moved together. They're both at the same column. So maybe these are just two visual indicators of the same cursor state.
Let me think about what the game might be. The cursor moves right (with UP) and transforms the symbol it lands on. Maybe the goal is to transform all symbols to match the grid cells.
But there are 5 P symbols and 6 P grid cells. So not all grid cells can match a unique symbol.
Let me reconsider. Maybe the cursor cycles through symbols, and UP/DOWN transforms the current symbol. The goal is to make all palette symbols match some grid cell pattern.
Actually, let me check: the cursor moved from P-symbol 0 to P-symbol 1. P-symbol 1 was transformed. Maybe the cursor was "selecting" P-symbol 0 initially, and UP moved it to P-symbol 1 and transformed P-symbol 1.
Or maybe the cursor was at P-symbol 0, and UP moved it to P-symbol 1 without transforming P-symbol 0. The transformation of P-symbol 1 happened because the cursor landed on it.
Let me try pressing UP again to see if the cursor moves to P-symbol 2 and transforms it.
